title: The Chemist Who Witnessed
dek: Italian Jewish chemist, Auschwitz survivor, and writer who turned survival into literature
mortality_event: Survived Auschwitz III-Monowitz (1944–45) before writing If This Is a Man and The Periodic Table

sources.name: Centro Internazionale di Studi Primo Levi: Biography

closing_line: The reprieve was one moment. The work was the rest of his life.
citation_passage: Primo Levi was an Italian Jewish chemist, writer, and Holocaust survivor from Turin. Arrested after joining a partisan group, he was deported to Auschwitz in 1944 and imprisoned at Monowitz. His chemical training led to work in a camp laboratory; help from the Italian civilian Lorenzo Perrone also mattered to his survival. After returning to Italy, he wrote If This Is a Man while rebuilding his working and family life. This eight-page biographical comic considers survival, testimony, and the responsibility of describing what happened. The Primo Levi study center's chronology connects his experience with his later writing.
